PullRequest.Title: Git - get the diff and num stats for a commit
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The command-line change and call paths are explicit: `--numstat` requires content diffs, all five built-in call sites discard the statistics, and each awaits this single Git subprocess (or runs it after ref changes). Exact wall-clock cost varies with repository/object-cache state and file contents, but the added work and scaling input are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocess CPU, blob/object reads, diff allocations, and additional numstat output bytes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the total bytes and diff complexity of all modified files in the compared range (and is incurred once per UI request or actual incoming-ref change), rather than primarily with the number/path metadata of changed entries as before.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased user-visible latency on commit/comparison/history actions and additional background CPU/I/O contention after ref changes.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Built-in file-list paths ran one metadata-only `git diff --name-status` (or `diff-tree --name-status` for the empty-tree case), so ordinary modified files did not require line-count computation before the UI could proceed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Git now computes line-count statistics for every changed blob during all ref/commit file-list requests, including built-in UI paths that only need change status and file names.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT extensions/git/src/git.ts:1771 replaces the prior metadata-only `git diff --name-status` implementation reached by `diffBetween2` with `git diff --raw --numstat`; the diff also migrates commands.ts, historyProvider.ts, and decorationProvider.ts to this method, although those callers only map status/URIs and never read the new counters.
Findings.Title: Avoid computing numstats for file-list-only callers
Findings.Impact: Opening a comparison/commit or expanding a history item's changes now waits for content diffs of the entire changed set; commits or incoming ranges containing large generated files, lockfiles, or many modified files can visibly delay the editor. Ref updates also repeat this work in the background for incoming decorations, creating avoidable Git CPU and disk/object-read pressure.
Findings.Evidence: Previously `diffBetween2` delegated to `diffFiles`, whose command is `git diff --name-status -z`; first-commit comparisons similarly used `diff-tree --name-status`. The new central command includes `--numstat`, which requires loading changed blobs and computing line diffs. `_openChangesBetweenRefs`, timeline/view-commit, `provideHistoryItemChanges`, and incoming decorations consume only `Change` fields through `toMultiFileDiffEditorUris` or status switches. Thus the line statistics are eagerly computed but unused on these paths.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a metadata-only diff method for callers that only need statuses/URIs and migrate these built-in call sites back to it; reserve `--numstat` for the new opt-in API or a caller that actually surfaces the counters. Preserve the existing single-process ordering and path filtering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a ref comparison, timeline commit, or SCM commit in the multi-diff editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits commit metadata as applicable, then awaits `Repository.diffBetweenWithStats`; the multi-diff editor is not opened until that Git process exits and all output is parsed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `git diff --raw --numstat --find-renames ...` (or `git diff-tree ... --raw --numstat` for an empty-tree parent), reading Git objects and computing content diffs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per open/compare request; inside the process, numstat work scales over every modified file in the selected commit/range.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed as one Git process, but it used `--name-status`; the diff materially increases the work inside that critical-path process by adding content-based numstat computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks construction and opening of the multi-diff editor.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one subprocess, with work controlled by total changed-file content bytes and diff complexity after Git's path/range filtering and rename processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Git diff process per command invocation; `Operation.Diff` is non-blocking/read-only and does not provide a limiter, though a normal user action starts one invocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no application result cache or coalescing. Warm Git/OS object caches can reduce reads, but every invocation recomputes line statistics; first-use cold packs are more expensive.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all relevant command call sites await the changed Git command and consume only status/URI fields, not the computed counters.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical small commits may show little difference; large generated files, lockfiles, or broad branch comparisons can make the additional content diff substantial.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression because eager, unused numstat computation was moved onto the editor-opening critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand an SCM history item to list its changed files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench requests changes over existing extension-host/main-thread IPC; the Git history provider awaits `diffBetweenWithStats`, builds URI/decorations, and only then returns the list over IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the changed numstat Git diff for the selected history item and parent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Git process per provider request, with internal content work across all changed files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider request ran one metadata-only `--name-status` process via `diffBetween2`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the history change list and any SCM multi-diff source resolution that depends on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the resulting history item change URI list from extension host to main thread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC response containing O(changed files) entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same URI/status-derived change list crossed IPC before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the critical path but its payload shape does not include the new numstat fields.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of returned change entries controls IPC size, while total changed content and diff complexity newly control subprocess latency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider request normally maps to one Git process. The provider receives a cancellation token but this implementation does not use it, so overlapping consumers can run independent requests; the PR did not introduce that concurrency behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provider-level result cache or request coalescing was found; OS/Git object caches are the only warm-cache benefit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the provider awaits the changed method and never reads insertions/deletions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency depends on history UI use and commit sizes; the mechanism is strongest on large-content commits.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported eager-work finding; no separate IPC finding because IPC cardinality and payload are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh incoming-change file decorations after repository/ref updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On provider construction and actual current/upstream ref changes, an async event handler resolves a merge base and runs the changed diff. The handler is not awaited by the write operation, so it is off that operation's direct critical path, but it competes for repository CPU/I/O before decorations update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the common ancestor, then run `git diff --raw --numstat` from that ancestor to the remote ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential Git processes per repository on initialization with available refs or on an actual current/upstream-ref change; only the second process is made more expensive by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same merge-base plus diff sequence existed, but the diff was metadata-only `--name-status` and did not compute line counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the write/fetch completion critical path, but blocks incoming decoration refresh and can contend with foreground Git/editor work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One changed ref pair per affected repository after equality suppression; numstat cost scales with total modified content in the incoming range.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within a repository, unchanged ref pairs are skipped and history write handling is throttled; actual ref changes launch one merge-base process followed by one diff process. Across open repositories these background chains may overlap, and `Operation.Diff` has no shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider retains the last ref identities and skips unchanged pairs, but it does not cache a prior diff result for a new pair. Warm object caches may reduce reads; line stats are recomputed on each real ref update.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added content-diff work and background reachability; user-visible contention magnitude varies by repository and update pattern.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Impact depends on number of repositories and size of incoming ranges; small repositories remain cheap, while monorepos or broad fetched ranges can create noticeable contention.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported finding as an automatic background amplification of the same unused numstat work; no separate concurrency-burst finding because realistic per-repository cardinality is bounded to actual ref changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension consumer explicitly requests diff changes with insertion/deletion statistics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new API implementation awaits one Git numstat subprocess; this work is required to produce the requested counters.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the new stats-producing Git diff, optionally narrowed by path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per API request; path filtering can reduce the effective changed set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No stats-returning API existed, so there was no equivalent request boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the API promise to resolve.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total bytes and diff complexity of modified files in the requested range after optional path filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One process per API call, with no application coalescing or limiter; concurrency is controlled by extension callers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache, negative cache, or coalescing exists; each explicit call recomputes stats. This is acceptable for a new opt-in operation whose result requires those stats.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one content diff is necessary and explicit on this opt-in path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unknown third-party call frequency and range sizes; callers can narrow by path.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not independently reportable: the new boundary is the requested API work. The regression comes from migrating existing file-list-only callers to it.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Found one central eager-work regression: adding `--numstat` to formerly metadata-only built-in paths forces unused blob line-diff computation on several critical/background scenarios. Checked process cardinality, IPC, caches, cancellation/coalescing, and cross-repository concurrency; no additional high-confidence performance findings or regression-fix learning signal were established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
